Box 4: Towards an e-KYC (Know-Your-Customer) registry To facilitate the opening of accounts in financial institutions for financially excluded populations, this digital data platform will host an e-KYC (Know-Your-Customer) registry.

The registry will help financial institutions to identify their customers and comply with Customer Due Diligence (CDD) regulation which constitute a key Page 62 of 89 The World Bank Niger: Smart Villages for Rural Growth and Digital Inclusion Project (P167543) component for compliance with AML/CFT requirements.
Indeed, high costs incurred by complex and time- consuming KYC controls and diligences are often considered as main barriers to financial inclusion.

According to a new regulation that will have to be adopted by the Minister of Finance before the creation of the e-KYC registry, the digital data platform held by ANSI will receive, store, safeguard and retrieve KYC records in a digital form for every client of financial institutions.

The e-KYC registry will be applicable in the first place only to individuals (population of Smart Villages) but could be extended to the entire population of Niger in the medium term.

evidence.text: Creation of digital centers network in rural areas – It is expected that the project will support the creation of 150 multi services digital centers by providing sub-grants for improvement of existing premises to house the centers, providing working capital (in the form of grants), training for the managers of the centers and helping to develop a business model that could allow the center to be sustainable even after the closing of the project.

extra_evidence.text: These centers will complement the existing mobile money agents in the targeted areas and will help fill the gaps while bringing additionality through more intensive support to customers.

A competitive process through a call for proposals to be launched by the PIU will allow to select three companies that will have the responsibility to select and manage the centers, and the sub-grants they would receive.

Digitization of payments received by the public agriculture input supplier, CAIMA or large input suppliers - Digitizing the agricultural value chain will involve digitizing the back-end processes at the CAIMA using an off-the-shelf ERP solution.

This ERP solution will record all the sales from CAIMA to the wholesalers and handle all the invoicing and payments related processes for the sales of agricultural inputs from CAIMA to the wholesalers.
The wholesalers themselves and retailers (stores and distribution outlets) would be equipped with digital payment solutions to receive digital payments from the farmers.
